feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 3.6, kd 0.6, mass 0.6 kg) scored 321, with oval finish 0.45 and s-bend finish 0.10. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m, kp 3.3) scored 303, with oval finish 0.65 but s-bend finish 0.00 and s-bend max_error rising to 0.0645 m. Sensing is not the limit: iteration 1's wider row cut line loss but lost completions. What I compensated for in the controller: narrowing the track raises yaw per unit of PWM difference, so kp is trimmed from 3.6 to 3.5 for this 0.095 m track, and kd is held at 0.6 to keep s-bend oscillation near 0.43. The next race should be read as follows. If s-bend finish rises above 0.05 and max_error falls below 0.063 m while the oval finish holds at or above 0.5, keep wheel_track near 0.095 m. If the s-bend stays at zero with max_error still about 0.0645 m, the overshoot is not set by turn authority, so the next lever is the sensor forward offset. If the oval finish drops to 0.45 or below, the track change is not the oval lever, so return to 0.10 m.
requested_changes: If the s-bend finish stays at 0 with max_error still about 0.0645 m, move the sensor row forward to y = 0.06 m with the same five sensors at ±0.04 m (0.02 m spacing). Evidence: iterations 2 and 3 both show s-bend max_error clustering at 0.0627 to 0.0645 m, so the sensors may be reacting too late at speed.

If the oval finish falls to 0.45 or below and completion_time worsens, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep mass 0.6 kg. Evidence: iteration 2 (0.10 m) reached 0.45 oval finish, and iteration 0 (0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg) reached only 0.05.

If the s-bend finish rises above 0.05 and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.43, keep wheel_track 0.095 m and test base_speed around 1.5 with kp unchanged. Evidence: the s-bend finish recovered in iteration 2 (0.10) when the track was wider, and speed is not yet the binding limit on the oval (finishers ran about 1.73 s).
